Read-only design task; do not edit or build. Repo: /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/wp-q-verify-real (Rust, callisto). Read AGENTS.md first (invariants, 'Enforcing an invariant' ladder, no cargo features in shipped crates, no source-scanning tests, new flags/codes are permanent).

Goal (work package Q, see /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md row Q): `just verify-real` rehearses, against LOCAL npm, cargo and PyPI registries, through PRODUCTION registry binding: (1) partial publish -> rerun adopts, (2) delayed visibility, (3) a conflicting tag, (4) a missing Python artifact. It must exit nonzero on any wrong outcome.

Blocker: crates/callisto-graph/src/registry_endpoint.rs `canonical_registry_url` rejects every non-https URL (no loopback exception, deliberate; a test asserts it). Callers: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/binding.rs (and config validation). Existing crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs (Linux only) works around this by driving registry_argv directly and routing via .npmrc/.cargo config, i.e. NOT through production binding.

Deliver a SHORT design (under 60 lines): (a) the narrowest test-only way past the https rule that keeps release builds unable to bind http (evaluate: runtime env var, a #[cfg(test)]-only path, the dev-only callisto-model/test-util feature precedent, TLS with a locally trusted self-signed cert via SSL_CERT_FILE/NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS/CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO/TWINE cert so NO production code change is needed -- check seriously whether TLS-local avoids touching registry_endpoint.rs at all; recommend one with reasons); (b) what local registries are realistically available on macOS and Linux with tools already installed or pip/npm-installable (verdaccio via npx, cargo-http-registry, pypiserver/devpi) and how the harness starts/stops them; (c) where the harness lives (justfile recipe + a Rust test target vs script; Callisto features go in Rust not shell per owner preference) and how scenarios (1)-(4) are driven through `callisto release execute` with the existing release_harness (crates/callisto-cli/tests/common/release_harness.rs); (d) the exact boundary test(s) and files to change, docs/specs to update (docs/architecture, docs/specs), and whether a changeset is needed (plan says no). Cite file:line for everything you rely on. Keep to the cheapest design that truly proves the four scenarios via production binding.

name: 'Install registry test tools'
description: 'Installs the local npm, PyPI and Cargo registries the real-registry e2e tests run against. Linux only; the tests fail without them under CI.'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Install Verdaccio (real-registry npm e2e coverage)
      if: runner.os == 'Linux'
      shell: bash
      run: npm install -g verdaccio@6.10.4 # zizmor: ignore[adhoc-packages] pinned to an exact upstream release; a CI-only test-registry tool, not a shipped or lockfile-tracked dependency.
    - name: Install pypiserver (real-registry PyPI e2e coverage)
      if: runner.os == 'Linux'
      shell: bash
      # legacy-cgi: pypiserver imports `cgi` (gone in 3.13). gunicorn: avoids a slow getfqdn() bind.
      # setuptools/wheel: the test builds with `--no-isolation`, so they must be pre-installed.
      run: | # zizmor: ignore[github-env] the PATH entry is a fixed child of the trusted runner temporary directory, not attacker-controlled input.
        python3 -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv"
        "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv/bin/pip" install pypiserver==2.4.0 twine==6.2.0 build==1.4.4 legacy-cgi==2.6.3 gunicorn==26.2.0 setuptools==80.9.0 wheel==0.45.1
        echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/pypi-e2e-venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
    - name: Install cargo-http-registry (real-registry Cargo e2e coverage)
      if: runner.os == 'Linux'
      shell: bash
      run: cargo install --locked cargo-http-registry@0.1.8 # zizmor: ignore[adhoc-packages] pinned to an exact upstream release; a CI-only test-registry tool, not a shipped or lockfile-tracked dependency.
.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml:59:        uses: $/.github/actions/install-registry-test-tools
.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml:130:        uses: $/.github/actions/install-registry-test-tools
fn skip_missing(what: &str) {
    assert!(
        std::env::var_os("CI").is_none() || std::env::var_os("CALLISTO_ALLOW_MISSING_TOOLS").is_some(),
        "{what}; the CI workflow must install it"
    );
    eprintln!("SKIPPED real-registry e2e: {what}");
}

In a 200 JSON body, any matching yanked file means absent; otherwise at least one matching non-yanked file means present. That version-level read serves every use outside an effect. Before a PyPI effect, `release execute` proceeds without a build when the index has no file of the version. Otherwise it builds, and treats the release as already satisfied only when every built file is on the index by filename and not yanked. A built file the index holds yanked is a remote conflict, and a file the index holds that the build did not produce is reported with a warning and not checked. After an upload, confirmation waits for every built file to be visible, and a file this run uploaded must carry the sha256 the index serves for it, or the run fails with E307. A file from an earlier attempt is matched by name, not by digest, unless the artifact manifest seals the release's files: then the run builds nothing, uploads those exact files, compares the sha256 of every file the index holds under a sealed name, and fails with E307 before any upload when one differs. A 404 or no matching file means absent, and a non-JSON body or other non-retryable status is indeterminate. Transient HTTP statuses use the observation retry policy."

input.message:
Design for work package Q (`just verify-real`). Read-only: I made no edits and ran no builds.

**(a) The https rule: use local TLS. No production code changes.**
- **Recommendation: TLS with a self-signed loopback cert.** I traced every network path, and callisto never opens a socket itself. There is no HTTP or TLS crate in Cargo.lock (no rustls, hyper or ureq). All registry traffic goes through child processes:
  - npm: `npm view` / `npm publish --registry <endpoint>` (provider/registry/npm.rs:138,174,209,232).
  - PyPI observation: `curl` (pypi.rs:194-205).
  - PyPI upload: `twine --repository-url` (registry_argv.rs:366-377).
  - cargo: only `--registry <key>` (cargo.rs:29-30,40,72).
- Providers inherit the environment. Nothing calls `env_clear`; only GIT_* variables are removed (callisto-model/src/vcs/access.rs:1174). The PyPI path only adds TWINE_* (pypi.rs:19-33). So the trust variables reach the tools:
  - `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` for npm.
  - `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` for curl, which twine's `requests` also honors.
  - `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` for twine.
- `canonical_registry_url` already accepts https on loopback (registry_endpoint.rs:77-102). The existing test accepts `https://[::1]:8765/` (registry_endpoint.rs:141-148).
- So `[registries.x] url = "https://127.0.0.1:<port>/..."` binds through the real `prepared_registry_binding` (binding.rs:57-121) unchanged. The http rule and its test (registry_endpoint.rs:124-138) stay as they are. That test's own doc comment says the loopback exception only ever existed for test harnesses.
- **Rejected options:**
  - A runtime env var would let a shipped binary send credentials in cleartext. `__CALLISTO_TEST_SLEEP_SCALE` (provider/policy.rs:186-194) is a precedent, but it only scales sleeps and cannot leak anything.
  - `#[cfg(test)]` does not apply to the CLI binary that the e2e tests spawn.
  - Extending the `test-util` feature: dev-deps unify features into the test build, so `CARGO_BIN_EXE_callisto` would accept http. It is also new feature surface against invariant 6.
- **Cert:** generated by the harness with the `openssl` CLI (present on macOS and Linux): `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 1 -subj /CN=localhost -addext subjectAltName=IP:127.0.0.1,DNS:localhost`. No new crate.
- **Spike first:** confirm macOS `/usr/bin/curl` (LibreSSL) honors `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, and twine 6.2 honors `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`. Fallback: put the harness's `fake-bin` ahead of curl on PATH. I'd treat that as last resort.
- **Cargo needs no TLS.** The cargo provider never reads `endpoint`; it passes only the key (cargo.rs:40,72). A `[registries.local-e2e] kind = "cargo"` entry is the full production binding for cargo. The http URL lives in `.cargo/config.toml`, as in the existing test (release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs:37-51).

**(b) Local registries (macOS and Linux). Pins already exist in .github/actions/install-registry-test-tools/action.yml:9,18,23.**
- **npm:** `npx --yes verdaccio@6.10.4`. Native TLS through its config: `listen: https://127.0.0.1:<port>` plus an `https: {key, cert}` block.
- **PyPI:** pypiserver 2.4.0 under gunicorn (already in the pin list), served directly so gunicorn terminates TLS: `gunicorn --certfile --keyfile -b 127.0.0.1:<port> "pypiserver:app(roots=[...], authenticate=[], password_file='.')"`. The app-factory arguments are a spike item. devpi has no native TLS, so it is not worth using.
- **cargo:** `cargo install --locked cargo-http-registry@0.1.8`, plain http and git index, with `net.git-fetch-with-cli = true` (as in the existing test).
- **Start/stop:** move `ServerGuard` (kill on Drop), `free_loopback_port`, `wait_for_port`, `start_verdaccio` and `start_pypiserver` from release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs:80-200,480-510,655-670 into `crates/callisto-cli/tests/common/local_registries.rs`. Add TLS variants and a `cert()` helper.
- **Tool provisioning:** a `verify-real-tools` just recipe installs into `target/verify-real/` (a venv plus `cargo install --root`). The CI action calls that recipe, so the pins live in one place.
- Locally I found only npx, uv, python3 and openssl. verdaccio, pypiserver, twine and cargo-http-registry are all missing, so the provisioning step is required.

**(c) Where the harness lives and how each scenario runs**
- **Justfile:** `verify-real: verify-real-tools` → `cargo test -p callisto-cli --test release_verify_real -- --ignored --test-threads=1` with the tools prepended to PATH.
- **Test file:** `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_verify_real.rs`, `#![cfg(unix)]`. Each test is `#[ignore = "needs local registries; run via just verify-real"]`. A missing tool panics rather than skipping (unlike `skip_missing`, :282), so any wrong outcome gives a nonzero exit. All logic stays in Rust; the shell only provisions tools.
- **Harness change:** add `real_publishers()` to release_harness.rs. It reuses the fake `git` (push plus the remote-tag store, release_harness.rs:546,1215-1232) and the fake `gh`, but writes no fake `cargo` (fake_publishers writes one, :535-541).
- **New `execute_real()`:** like `execute` (:574-608) but without `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN=REDACTED or `CALLISTO_TEST_CARGO_MARKER`. It sets the CA variables, `TWINE_USERNAME`/`TWINE_PASSWORD`, `CARGO_HOME` (holding the `.cargo` config and token) and `__CALLISTO_TEST_SLEEP_SCALE=0.1`. The origin stays `https://github.com/...` (:183), which passes the git-remote rule.
- **Scenario 0 (proves the binding is production):** the same workspace with `url = "http://127.0.0.1:<port>"` fails with E126 before any effect (spec docs/specs/release.json:222).
- **(1) Partial publish, then rerun adopts:** npm packages `a` and `b`, where `b` depends on `a`. They bind to two npm-kind `[registries]` entries, each its own TLS verdaccio. In run 1, `b`'s registry is not started, so the run fails and writes no receipt. Run 2 starts it and must:
  - exit 0 and write a receipt;
  - show `a ... is already published; skipping` on stderr (spec :285);
  - leave registry 1 with `a` exactly once and registry 2 with `b`.
  - The cargo variant: crate `core` bound to a key-only `local-e2e` entry whose `.cargo` config points at a port not yet listening in run 1.
- **(2) Delayed visibility:** PyPI split routes. `url` is index server I (`https://127.0.0.1:I/simple`), `publish-url` is upload server U (spec :235), each a pypiserver on its own directory. A test thread copies U's directory into I's after about 3 s. With `confirm-timeout = "30s"`, the run must succeed after more than one look (spec :239). A variant that never copies must exit with E157 and no receipt; a rerun after the copy adopts.
- **(3) Conflicting tag:** seed `$CALLISTO_TEST_GIT_TRACE.remote-tags` with `<pkg>@<ver>` pointing at another object. The run must exit with E167, write no receipt, and never adopt the tag (spec :293). Whether the registry is untouched depends on when tags are checked relative to effects; read that ordering from the code at implementation time.
- **(4) Missing Python artifact:** seed index directory I (or U and I together) with the sdist only. Then `release execute` must upload just the wheel, end with both files on the index, and leave the sdist unchanged. Twine never passes `--skip-existing` (registry_argv.rs:366-372), so if callisto re-uploaded the sdist, pypiserver would refuse it and the run would fail. Success itself proves only the missing file was sent.

**(d) Files, tests and docs**
- **Production code:** none. The boundary tests stay unchanged: registry_endpoint.rs:124 (http rejected, loopback included) and :141 (https accepted).
- **New:**
  - `tests/release_verify_real.rs`
  - `tests/common/local_registries.rs`
  - `real_publishers` / `execute_real` in `tests/common/release_harness.rs`
  - justfile `verify-real` and `verify-real-tools` recipes
  - action.yml calls `just verify-real-tools`.
- **Edit release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs:12-34:** its header says a loopback registry "can never be configured", which TLS now makes false. Repoint it at the shared helpers. Optional, owner's call: delete its argv-level PyPI and cargo tests as superseded and run `just verify-real` in the Linux CI job instead.
- **Docs:**
  - AGENTS.md Commands: one bullet for `just verify-real`.
  - docs/architecture/release.md: one line naming the rehearsal and the local-TLS approach.
  - docs/specs: no change. The harness is not product behavior, and release.json:222 stays true.
- **Changeset:** none (not user-visible), as the plan says.

**Risks to spike first, all cheap:**
- macOS curl honoring `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`.
- twine honoring `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`.
- The `pypiserver:app` keyword arguments under gunicorn.
- verdaccio's https config.
- Execution order in scenario (1), i.e. that `a` is issued before `b` fails. Check that callisto orders npm packages by dependency.

**(a) The https rule: use local TLS. No production code changes.**
- **Recommendation: TLS with a self-signed loopback cert.** I traced every network path, and callisto never opens a socket itself. There is no HTTP or TLS crate in Cargo.lock (no rustls, hyper or ureq). All registry traffic goes through child processes:
  - npm: `npm view` / `npm publish --registry <endpoint>` (provider/registry/npm.rs:138,174,209,232).
  - PyPI observation: `curl` (pypi.rs:194-205).
  - PyPI upload: `twine --repository-url` (registry_argv.rs:366-377).
  - cargo: only `--registry <key>` (cargo.rs:29-30,40,72).
- Providers inherit the environment. Nothing calls `env_clear`; only GIT_* variables are removed (callisto-model/src/vcs/access.rs:1174). The PyPI path only adds TWINE_* (pypi.rs:19-33). So the trust variables reach the tools:
  - `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` for npm.
  - `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` for curl, which twine's `requests` also honors.
  - `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` for twine.
- `canonical_registry_url` already accepts https on loopback (registry_endpoint.rs:77-102). The existing test accepts `https://[::1]:8765/` (registry_endpoint.rs:141-148).
- So `[registries.x] url = "https://127.0.0.1:<port>/..."` binds through the real `prepared_registry_binding` (binding.rs:57-121) unchanged. The http rule and its test (registry_endpoint.rs:124-138) stay as they are. That test's own doc comment says the loopback exception only ever existed for test harnesses.
- **Rejected options:**
  - A runtime env var would let a shipped binary send credentials in cleartext. `__CALLISTO_TEST_SLEEP_SCALE` (provider/policy.rs:186-194) is a precedent, but it only scales sleeps and cannot leak anything.
  - `#[cfg(test)]` does not apply to the CLI binary that the e2e tests spawn.
  - Extending the `test-util` feature: dev-deps unify features into the test build, so `CARGO_BIN_EXE_callisto` would accept http. It is also new feature surface against invariant 6.
- **Cert:** generated by the harness with the `openssl` CLI (present on macOS and Linux): `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 1 -subj /CN=localhost -addext subjectAltName=IP:127.0.0.1,DNS:localhost`. No new crate.
- **Spike first:** confirm macOS `/usr/bin/curl` (LibreSSL) honors `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, and twine 6.2 honors `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`. Fallback: put the harness's `fake-bin` ahead of curl on PATH. I'd treat that as last resort.
- **Cargo needs no TLS.** The cargo provider never reads `endpoint`; it passes only the key (cargo.rs:40,72). A `[registries.local-e2e] kind = "cargo"` entry is the full production binding for cargo. The http URL lives in `.cargo/config.toml`, as in the existing test (release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs:37-51).

**(b) Local registries (macOS and Linux). Pins already exist in .github/actions/install-registry-test-tools/action.yml:9,18,23.**
- **npm:** `npx --yes verdaccio@6.10.4`. Native TLS through its config: `listen: https://127.0.0.1:<port>` plus an `https: {key, cert}` block.
- **PyPI:** pypiserver 2.4.0 under gunicorn (already in the pin list), served directly so gunicorn terminates TLS: `gunicorn --certfile --keyfile -b 127.0.0.1:<port> "pypiserver:app(roots=[...], authenticate=[], password_file='.')"`. The app-factory arguments are a spike item. devpi has no native TLS, so it is not worth using.
- **cargo:** `cargo install --locked cargo-http-registry@0.1.8`, plain http and git index, with `net.git-fetch-with-cli = true` (as in the existing test).
- **Start/stop:** move `ServerGuard` (kill on Drop), `free_loopback_port`, `wait_for_port`, `start_verdaccio` and `start_pypiserver` from release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs:80-200,480-510,655-670 into `crates/callisto-cli/tests/common/local_registries.rs`. Add TLS variants and a `cert()` helper.
- **Tool provisioning:** a `verify-real-tools` just recipe installs into `target/verify-real/` (a venv plus `cargo install --root`). The CI action calls that recipe, so the pins live in one place.
- Locally I found only npx, uv, python3 and openssl. verdaccio, pypiserver, twine and cargo-http-registry are all missing, so the provisioning step is required.

**(c) Where the harness lives and how each scenario runs**
- **Justfile:** `verify-real: verify-real-tools` → `cargo test -p callisto-cli --test release_verify_real -- --ignored --test-threads=1` with the tools prepended to PATH.
- **Test file:** `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_verify_real.rs`, `#![cfg(unix)]`. Each test is `#[ignore = "needs local registries; run via just verify-real"]`. A missing tool panics rather than skipping (unlike `skip_missing`, :282), so any wrong outcome gives a nonzero exit. All logic stays in Rust; the shell only provisions tools.
- **Harness change:** add `real_publishers()` to release_harness.rs. It reuses the fake `git` (push plus the remote-tag store, release_harness.rs:546,1215-1232) and the fake `gh`, but writes no fake `cargo` (fake_publishers writes one, :535-541).
- **New `execute_real()`:** like `execute` (:574-608) but without `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN=REDACTED or `CALLISTO_TEST_CARGO_MARKER`. It sets the CA variables, `TWINE_USERNAME`/`TWINE_PASSWORD`, `CARGO_HOME` (holding the `.cargo` config and token) and `__CALLISTO_TEST_SLEEP_SCALE=0.1`. The origin stays `https://github.com/...` (:183), which passes the git-remote rule.
- **Scenario 0 (proves the binding is production):** the same workspace with `url = "http://127.0.0.1:<port>"` fails with E126 before any effect (spec docs/specs/release.json:222).
- **(1) Partial publish, then rerun adopts:** npm packages `a` and `b`, where `b` depends on `a`. They bind to two npm-kind `[registries]` entries, each its own TLS verdaccio. In run 1, `b`'s registry is not started, so the run fails and writes no receipt. Run 2 starts it and must:
  - exit 0 and write a receipt;
  - show `a ... is already published; skipping` on stderr (spec :285);
  - leave registry 1 with `a` exactly once and registry 2 with `b`.
  - The cargo variant: crate `core` bound to a key-only `local-e2e` entry whose `.cargo` config points at a port not yet listening in run 1.
- **(2) Delayed visibility:** PyPI split routes. `url` is index server I (`https://127.0.0.1:I/simple`), `publish-url` is upload server U (spec :235), each a pypiserver on its own directory. A test thread copies U's directory into I's after about 3 s. With `confirm-timeout = "30s"`, the run must succeed after more than one look (spec :239). A variant that never copies must exit with E157 and no receipt; a rerun after the copy adopts.
- **(3) Conflicting tag:** seed `$CALLISTO_TEST_GIT_TRACE.remote-tags` with `<pkg>@<ver>` pointing at another object. The run must exit with E167, write no receipt, and never adopt the tag (spec :293). Whether the registry is untouched depends on when tags are checked relative to effects; read that ordering from the code at implementation time.
- **(4) Missing Python artifact:** seed index directory I (or U and I together) with the sdist only. Then `release execute` must upload just the wheel, end with both files on the index, and leave the sdist unchanged. Twine never passes `--skip-existing` (registry_argv.rs:366-372), so if callisto re-uploaded the sdist, pypiserver would refuse it and the run would fail. Success itself proves only the missing file was sent.
